delete.description: Deletes the account, its passkeys and tokens. Commits already made keep the public handle.

patch.description:
Opt in to (or out of) nudge emails: a reminder when you haven't stored a card in a while. Opting in shares
your handle, role and email with the team's mailing list.

get.description: Everyone on the team, the people waiting to be let in first.

delete.description:
Removes someone from the team: their account is closed and every sign-in revoked at once. Their
handle stays reserved, since commits they made carry it.

post.description: Let someone in: they see the team's work from their next request. Turning someone away is removing them.

Signed in: add a passkey to this account. Signed out, with a handle and an invite: create an
account whose first sign-in method is this passkey (the invite is used up when it is verified).
Add or change the account's email + password. Changing one needs the current password.

delete.description: No more notifications in this browser.

subscription moves to whoever turns notifications on in that browser last.

get.description: The key a browser subscribes with (applicationServerKey): this server's VAPID public key, base64url.

post.description: A test notification to every browser you turned notifications on in. Counts come back.

get.description:
`topic`, `file` and `block` filter by slug and name, as the apps know them. `brief`: the cards scanned from
that brief, in page order.

delete.description: Archive: the file is deleted in a commit; history keeps every version.

get.description: Cards whose files link to this one.

post.description: Model suggestions are pending spans in the index; accepting one commits it to the card file.

With `content`, commit sources/<n>.md as sent. With only `url`, the server reads the article
and commits its clean text.

get.description: Who a name could be: the team's knowledge base first, then Wikidata's own search for the rest.

post.description: A finished round, from the timer: its times, what was opened when, and the notes. One commit.

A ticket to the shared service where live rounds run (scythe-ocr's rounds.py): this team, this member, this
round (or `*`: any of the team's, to list them), for twelve hours. The clock itself never comes through here.

A photo of a printed card, read by OCR on this server into a draft: `tag`, `cite`, `body`, `text` (all three:
what becomes the source), `markdown`, and `spans`: the underlines, highlights and emphasis read off the paper, over
`body`. With `quad` (a JSON list of 8 numbers: the card's corners, TL TR BR BL, in the photo the app took), the
photo must be the app's warp of those corners to the card's flat frame; it's then also turned upright. The photo
is read in memory and never stored: no file, row or commit, and only the text goes back.

get.description: Your briefs being scanned or checked, newest first, with their pages' progress.

post.description: Start scanning a brief under `name`: its pages are sent to POST /scan/pages with this brief's id.

delete.description: Discard the brief: its pages and every card of it still waiting.

post.description:
Save every card of the brief still waiting, as they are: each becomes a source and a card cut from it, with
the brief's name and the card's pages as its `brief`, all in one commit. Refused (409) while a page is still
being read: wait for it, or drop it.

get.description:
Your cards waiting to be checked: by brief (newest first), in page order; then pages scanned on their own,
newest first.

delete.description: Discard a card without saving it.

patch.description:
Fix the tag or cite, or mark the words: `spans` replaces the card's marks (underline, highlight, emphasis over
`body`, UTF-16 offsets on whole characters). The words themselves stay as read: the card keeps them exactly.

post.description:
Join the next card (the one after it on its page, or the first of the next page of the brief) onto this one:
this card's tag and cite stay, the words follow as another paragraph, with their marks.

Save the card: what was read becomes its source, and the card is cut from it word for word, with its marks,
tag and cite, filed under `topic` (or your current one); a card from a brief carries the brief and its pages.

Split the card at `at` (a UTF-16 offset into `body`, moved to the end of the word it lands in): the words
before stay this card; the words from there become a new card after it, with the same cite and no tag.

A page to read: a `screenshot` (read as it is) or a `photo` of paper at any angle (this server finds the
page's four corners, squares it up, turns it upright, then reads it; send `corners`, a JSON list of 8 fractions
of the upright picture, TL TR BR BL, to say where they are). Answers at once (202): the page is queued, and GET
/scan/pages/{id} says when it's read and which cards it gave. `brief` and `ordinal` (its page number, 1-based;
the next one when left out) file it under a brief. The picture is read in memory and never kept.

delete.description: Drop the page and the cards read off it (a card that ran over from the page before keeps its own part).

get.description: The page's state: ask again every couple of seconds while it's `queued` or `reading`.

post.description:
Read the page again, from the picture as the other kind or from corners the member dragged: its cards are
replaced when it's read (a card joined from the page before keeps its other part).

A scan that failed on the member's phone before it reached this server (the camera, the scanner script, the
picture, or the upload): `step` where, `message` what the phone said, `agent` its browser. Written to this
server's log only, so the team's operator can see a failure that never left the phone.

get.description:
Cards: `q` is Google's syntax ("a phrase", -word, a OR b; the last word matches as a prefix while it's being
typed), matched in tiers: the phrase, then every word, then any word. `sort=best` orders by tier, then
rank; `recent` by the last change; `published` by the source's date, newest first. `month` (2024-03) keeps cards
whose source was published that month.

Every card that quotes or names a person: cards whose words name them (spaCy's PERSON names; the surname alone
counts) and cards cut from a source they wrote. Names match ignoring case and "Last, First" order.

--paths.train train.spacy --paths.dev dev.spacy`.
Topics you have cards under first, then custom ones, then newest seasons.
